dct_description_sm: Northwest Territories (NWT) communities and aboriginal people in particular have a close relationship to the land and forests. Healthy forests and landscapes are integral to maintain safe and sustainable communities. Recent warming trends have allowed a new insect species to migrate north. The Mountain Pine Beetle (MPB) is the most destructive insect of pine trees in North America and has the potential to affect forest health across entire landscapes and in turn affect community health.   If MPB were to spread across southern NWT, its impacts on aboriginal people, communities, wildlife habitat, fire hazards and the forest industry are not known. Based on the experiences of BC and Alberta, NWT is concerned that MPB could have devastating effects on communities with respect to increased fire hazard, altering boreal caribou habitat and other key animals used as part of traditional lifestyles. It is important that the Government of NWT remains proactive in identifying the risk of MPB. This project aimed to predict the potential for MPB to establish, spread and impact the pine forest of southern NWT, identify achievable objectives to mitigate and minimize negative impacts of MPB, and communicate current and predicted status of MPB to communities and affected stakeholders.
